title: Carnival Night
subtitle: Mardi Gras: A City in Masks, a Serpent by Flambeau Light, the Captain's Room at Midnight

setting.name: New Orleans, Mardi Gras, Tuesday 5 March 1946
setting.description: The first Mardi Gras since 1941. The whole city is on the street from dawn, masked and costumed; the morning parades roll on St. Charles Avenue and Canal Street; the courts, banks and post office are closed and nothing can be filed, recorded or mailed until Wednesday. The Krewe of Oneiros forms up at its den, a cotton warehouse on Tchoupitoulas Street, at 5 p.m., rolls at 6:30 by flambeau light up to Lee Circle and down St. Charles Avenue to Canal Street, along Canal and up to the Municipal Auditorium at the edge of Tremé, where its floats are parked in the yard behind the building and its ball begins at 9. At midnight the police sweep Canal Street and Carnival is over.
setting.atmosphere: A city that has decided to be happy for one day after four years of war, and means it: brass bands on every corner, sailors and soldiers in costume, whole families in matching masks, children on ladders with boxes on top to see over the crowd, men selling roasted peanuts and paper horns, the smell of beer, fried dough, horse dung, naphtha and cigar smoke. At dusk the flambeaux are lit, and the floats come down St. Charles Avenue as towers of colored light, each led by its mule team, with masked riders throwing trinkets into a forest of raised hands, and between the floats the flambeaux carriers, Black men in white robes dancing with flaming naphtha torches on poles, catching the coins the crowd throws at their feet. It is gorgeous and it is a pageant of who rules whom. Let the players feel both. The tone is a thriller in a crowd: everyone is masked, the killer is somewhere on a float, and nothing is quiet until midnight.

keyLocations.name: The Oneiros Den, Tchoupitoulas Street
keyLocations.description: A long brick cotton warehouse near the river where the floats stand from Monday night until the parade forms up at 5 p.m. on Mardi Gras. The krewe's watchmen (four of Gravier's men in armbands, and Clovis Pinac, lent by Honoré) guard the doors; the krewe's riders arrive from 4:30 to robe and mask in a back room; the mule teams and their Black drivers wait in the street; the flambeaux carriers gather in the alley to fill their torches with naphtha.
features: Float fourteen, The Leviathan, standing between the kraken and the mermaid's grotto
The robing room, with eighteen racks of costumes and masks, nine per float, each on a hook with a number
The alley, where the flambeaux carriers and the mule drivers wait, and the krewe's watchmen do not look
Pinac's stool by the main door, with Bijou
encounters: Clovis Pinac and four krewe watchmen (Night Watchman, Dockside Goons), all afternoon
Riders of the Krewe of Oneiros arriving to robe, from 4:30
Theo Dorsainville's welders, hired as flambeaux carriers for the night
secrets: CLUE H2 (core, automatic if the party tells Pinac that Lucien did not kill Marcel, or if Yvonne asks him, or if anyone asks him who he moved the car for and why): Pinac breaks. 'I moved the car for Mr. Honoré, six-thirty Friday morning, and I tore out the page. He said Mr. Lucien's people had done a terrible thing and the family must not pay for it. Mr. Honoré has never in his life asked me to do a wrong thing before.' He believes Lucien had it done. He is appalled to hear that perhaps nobody in the family did.

Costume hook fourteen-three holds a Triton's robe of green satin and a silver-scaled mask; its rider has not arrived by 5:30 because he has already robed at his hotel. It is Pruett's. A spare robe and mask on hook fourteen-nine belong to a rider who is sick with influenza; anyone of the right height can take his place on the float (Deception DC 12 to pass the krewe lieutenant, advantage for anyone in a mask on Masking Day).

Before 5 p.m., the packet is still under the third scale from the tail on the Leviathan's port side, unless the party took it on Monday. The den is guarded but the watchmen are drinking by 3; a search takes one scene and needs a distraction or a disguise (Stealth or Deception DC 13; Heat +2 if caught).

keyLocations.name: The Pichon House, Annette Street
keyLocations.description: Anatole Pichon's raised Creole cottage in the Seventh Ward, with his plaster shop in the back yard under a tin roof. On Mardi Gras morning his wife, Mrs. Odette Pichon, keeps a pot of gumbo on the stove for whoever climbs the steps, and the plasterers who built the Oneiros floats, off duty and in their Sunday clothes, sit on the porch rail and watch the Seventh Ward's own parades go by.
features: The porch, the gumbo pot and the plasterers, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m.
The plaster shop: the clay maquette of the Leviathan, a foot long, with every scale numbered in pencil
Zélie's room at the back, if she is played
encounters: Anatole and Odette Pichon, and five or six of Pichon's plasterers including Martial Sauvinet
secrets: CLUE G1 (core, automatic for Zélie, Theo or Anatole Pichon, or for anyone they bring who sits down and eats before asking): Martial Sauvinet, plasterer, remembers Thursday night in the mold loft. The big Navy man who was helping dress the serpent went out at a quarter to nine and came back at ten with his trouser cuffs soaked and orange paint on his shoes, red lead from the fitting-out pier, and asked for a rag and some turpentine, and was very cheerful. 'Like a man who had just won at cards.'
The maquette: scale 3 from the tail on the port side is pencilled '3P'. Pichon can show anyone which scale it is on the real float in a minute.

keyLocations.name: The Parade Route: Lee Circle, St. Charles Avenue and Canal Street
keyLocations.description: From the den the procession turns up to Lee Circle and rolls down St. Charles Avenue between crowds twenty deep, past the hotels, to Canal Street, where it turns along the widest street in America, packed from storefront to storefront, and then away up toward the Municipal Auditorium. It halts every few blocks when the floats ahead halt, or when a mule balks, or when the krewe's mounted lieutenants call it. The parade takes about two hours.
features: The halts: about every three blocks, two to five minutes each; the long halt at Canal and St. Charles, eight minutes, while the floats turn
The flambeaux: one carrier walks on each side of every float; the naphtha torches can be swung, dipped or dropped
Balconies and ladders: the hotels' balconies on St. Charles are rented by the seat, and the crowd stands on ladders and boxes
Police lines at the corners; Det. Lamarque on the parade detail at Lee Circle, by Captain Lebeau's order
encounters: Commander Pruett, masked, on float fourteen
Six of Gravier's men in the crowd near Canal Street (Dockside Goons and Street Toughs), told to watch for the party
Beat Cops at every corner; mounted krewe lieutenants on horseback
secrets: Pruett's plan: during the long halt at Canal and St. Charles, while the other riders of float fourteen throw to the crowd, he climbs down the inside of the coil to the tail, cuts the third scale from the port side with a pocket knife, takes the packet, and drops it into the flambeau of the carrier walking alongside, whom he has paid five dollars to hold the torch steady. The carrier is one of Theo's welders, if Theo has been told; if not, it is a stranger who does as he is paid.

Recognising Pruett among nine masked Tritons on the float: DC 15 Insight or Perception, with advantage for anyone who has watched his hands (the heavy gold Navy ring) or his height. Or simpler: he is the only rider on float fourteen not throwing anything.
If the party took the packet already, Pruett spends the halt looking for them in the crowd, and Gravier's men try to take it from whoever has it on Canal Street.

keyLocations.name: The Municipal Auditorium and the Oneiros Ball
keyLocations.description: The great auditorium at the edge of Tremé, transformed into the bottom of the sea: a ballroom floor hung with green and silver gauze, the Queen's throne of silver shells on the stage, tiers of boxes full of white families in evening dress, the call-out section where women sit with their numbers waiting to be called to dance by masked krewe members, a society orchestra, and an army of Black waiters, maids and porters working the night. Admission is by engraved invitation and is for white guests only. Behind the stage is the captain's room, where the masked krewe men go to unmask and drink, and behind the building is the float yard, where the eighteen floats are parked after the parade with their flambeaux put out.
features: The call-out section, the Queen's court and the grand march at 10
The captain's room behind the stage: a door with a krewe lieutenant on it, a bar, a long table, the captain's chair, a window onto the float yard
The service corridor, the kitchen and the waiters' stairs, which go everywhere
The float yard behind the building: eighteen dark floats, mule teams being led away, a gate onto St. Claude Avenue, and two watchmen
encounters: Yvonne Ste. Claire, Queen of Oneiros, from 9
Honoré Ste. Claire, in the founder's box
Lucien Ste. Claire, the captain, masked until 11 and then in the captain's room
Commander Pruett, unmasked, from about 9:30
Captain Lebeau, as a guest
secrets: CLUE G5 (core, automatic for anyone who overhears it: from the service corridor, from the window over the float yard, from behind the captain's bar as a waiter, or through Yvonne, who is allowed anywhere tonight): at about 11:15, in the captain's room, Lucien, drunk and unmasked, says to Pruett, 'You told me he would not be a problem.' Pruett: 'And he isn't.' Lucien: 'My father thinks I did it. My father had his car moved.' Pruett: 'Then your father thinks you did it, Lucien. Let him. It's the most useful thing he's ever thought.' Lucien understands, in that moment, and the party may see him understand.

CLUE H1 (core, for anyone who asks Captain Lebeau's driver, a talkative patrolman named Rigaud, waiting outside with the car, or Det. Lamarque, who can read the switchboard log; see cs-scenario-002): Honoré telephoned the captain at home at 6:10 on Friday morning, two hours before the body had a name. Rigaud drove the captain to Esplanade Avenue at seven.

CLUE H3 (core, automatic from Yvonne, who can find the party anywhere in the building tonight): she repeats, word for word, the two telephone calls she heard on Saturday, her father's 'I never told anyone to touch him, Emile, I told you to find the papers' and her grandfather's 'My son is a fool, Achille, not a murderer, and I will not see him tried for it'. Laid beside Pinac's confession (H2) and Lucien's words at the Isabeau (H4), it means what she has not yet let herself see: each man believes the other did it.
Honoré does not know about gang No. 9. If the party tells him at the ball, he does not believe them, and then, from the look on Lucien's face across the room, he does.

keyLocations.name: The Café Isabeau, Bourbon Street
keyLocations.description: A small, smoky club with a horseshoe bar, a bandstand for a five-piece band and a singer, red banquettes, and a back room where Carnival men bring women who are not their wives. Solange Delery sings here, but not on Mardi Gras night, when the club is packed with masked strangers and the band plays until the sweep. Its bartender, Ulysse, has worked here since Repeal.
features: The back booth where Lucien Ste. Claire drank four double ryes at 11:30 Thursday night
Ulysse's memory, which is perfect, and his price, which is a good tip
A telephone booth by the cloakroom
encounters: Ulysse, bartender
Lucien Ste. Claire, after midnight, if he leaves the ball and comes here, as he sometimes does
secrets: CLUE H4 (core, automatic from Ulysse for Solange or anyone she sends, or from Solange herself if she is played): on Thursday night Lucien sat in the back booth white as paper and said, to no one, 'The old man always cleans up after me. He'll clean this up too.' On Saturday he came in again and said it again to Solange, crying.

If Lucien comes here after midnight on Mardi Gras, having heard Pruett in the captain's room, he is ready to talk to Solange, and to nobody else. He says he will go to his father in the morning. (In cs-scenario-004 he does.)

keyLocations.name: Terminal Station, Canal Street at Basin
keyLocations.description: The Southern Railway's terminal at the lake end of Canal Street, a brick building with a clock tower, a waiting room for white passengers and a smaller waiting room for Black passengers, and a baggage room open all night. The Crescent Limited leaves for New York at 1:15 p.m. on Ash Wednesday.
features: The baggage room counter, the claim checks, and an elderly clerk who has worked nights here since 1922
The two waiting rooms
A ticket window, where a first-class ticket to New York was bought on Monday in the name of T. W. Pruett
encounters: Commander Pruett, at about 12:20 a.m., if anyone tails him from the ball
The night baggage clerk, Mr. Oscar Nunez
secrets: At about 12:20 a.m., after the sweep, Pruett checks a heavy brown leather valise at the baggage room, claim check 4471, and puts the check in his wallet. It holds the photostats, $9,000 in cash and his Navy papers. (This sets up Clue G3 in cs-scenario-004. A tail from the ball, especially by a Shadow, sees him do it.)
A first-class ticket on the Wednesday Crescent Limited to New York was bought on Monday in Pruett's name.

synopsis: Mardi Gras, 1946. The whole city is masked, the courts and banks are closed, and nothing can be filed or mailed until tomorrow. The proof Marcel Fontenot died for, the Navy-copy pay summaries, is wrapped in oilcloth under the third scale from the tail on the port side of the Leviathan, float fourteen of the Krewe of Oneiros, standing under guard in a cotton warehouse on Tchoupitoulas Street; and Commander Thaddeus Pruett, who killed Marcel for it, has had himself assigned to ride on that float tonight, masked as a Triton. In the afternoon the party can try for the packet at the den, and can break the old watchman who moved Marcel's car, and learn that Honoré Ste. Claire believes his son is a murderer. At dusk the flambeaux are lit and Theo Dorsainville's laid-off welders, hired to carry them for a dollar and a half and the coins thrown at their feet, walk beside the floats down St. Charles Avenue, and during the long halt at Canal Street Pruett climbs down inside the serpent's coil to take the packet and burn it in a flambeau. Whoever holds it then must get it through a packed Canal Street, past Gravier's men, to somewhere safe. At the ball in the Municipal Auditorium, where the yard owner's granddaughter is Queen of Carnival and only white guests are admitted, the party overhears the killer and the captain of the krewe in the captain's room, and Lucien Ste. Claire learns that the man he thought had bought off his clerk killed him, and that his father has been protecting him from a crime he did not commit. At midnight the police sweep Canal Street, the masks come off, and Pruett checks a valise at Terminal Station.
hook: Mardi Gras, Tuesday 5 March 1946. You wake to brass bands. Under your window a man dressed as a chicken is playing the trombone, and two sailors dressed as nuns are dancing with a woman dressed as the Statue of Liberty, and at the corner a family of seven in identical green masks is waiting for the streetcar that will not run today, because nothing runs today, because it is Carnival. The courts are shut. The banks are shut. The post office is shut. By nightfall half a million people will be on St. Charles Avenue and Canal Street to see the night parades, and somewhere among the floats of the Krewe of Oneiros, in the belly of a papier-mâché sea serpent forty feet long, is the thing a pay clerk died for, and riding on top of it in a silver mask will be the man who killed him. You have until the flambeaux are lit.

conclusions.conclusion: G. Commander Thaddeus Pruett killed Marcel Fontenot (first proof)
clues: G1: Pichon's plasterers: Pruett left the mold loft at 8:45 Thursday and came back at 10 with wet cuffs and red lead on his shoes (the den, the plasterers)
G4: Marcel's notebook 'Cmdr — Thurs 9 — fitting-out pier' and Sallis's 'T.P. advised' (from cs-scenario-002)
G5: Pruett to Lucien in the captain's room: 'Your father thinks you did it. Let him.' (the Municipal Auditorium)
B2 from cs-scenario-001: CMDR PRUETT in on foot at 18:30 on the night of the murder; the navy serge fibre and the killer's height and handedness from the morgue

conclusions.conclusion: H. Each Ste. Claire believes the other killed Marcel, and each is covering for him
clues: H1: Honoré's 6:10 a.m. call to Captain Lebeau, before the body had a name (the 5th District switchboard log; Lebeau's driver)
H2: Pinac moved the car and tore the log page on Honoré's order, believing Lucien guilty (the den)
H3: Yvonne heard Lucien tell Gravier he never ordered anyone touched, and Honoré tell Lebeau his son is no murderer (Yvonne)
H4: Lucien: 'The old man always cleans up after me' (the Café Isabeau)

acts.title: Act 1: Masking Day
acts.description: Mardi Gras morning to 6 p.m. The city is a party and every street downtown is a crowd. The party has the day to prepare: try for the packet at the den on Tchoupitoulas Street before 5, break Clovis Pinac (H2), learn from Pichon's plasterers what they saw on Thursday night (G1), and make a plan for the parade with Theo, whose welders will be carrying the flambeaux. Masks are legal today: anyone in costume is anonymous (see campaignRules, Masking Day). Det. Lamarque, if played, is on parade detail at Lee Circle from 4 by Lebeau's order and must choose whether to leave his post. Pruett spends the morning at the Hotel Vauclain and robes there at 4.
objectives: Decide whether to try for the packet at the den, or on the route
Learn who moved Marcel's car and why
Hear what the plasterers saw on Thursday night
Agree a plan with Theo and the flambeaux carriers

scenes.name: A City in Masks
scenes.description: Morning in the street. The day parades (Rex, the real king of Carnival, and the others) are public events the party can watch or cross; they are background, not story. Use the morning to show the city's joy and its order at the same time: the Black and white crowds on separate stretches of the same avenue by custom; the colored cab stopped at the St. Claude bridge; a Black family's own costumes and a social aid and pleasure club's parade in the Seventh Ward, which is theirs and is not the white krewes' business; children everywhere. Plasterers from Pichon's shop, in costume and off duty, can be found at Pichon's house on Annette Street, where his wife has made a pot of gumbo for whoever comes: G1 is here (see the scene check). Give the party a quiet moment in the noise before the night.
scenes.readAloud: The Seventh Ward is dancing. On North Claiborne Avenue, under the oaks, a social club's own parade comes past in pale blue suits and straw hats with ribbons, with a brass band and a crowd of two hundred following it, and a man with a parasol at the front who seems to have been born dancing, and nobody here is looking at St. Charles Avenue at all. On the Pichons' porch on Annette Street an old woman is ladling gumbo into bowls for anyone who climbs the steps, and the plasterers who built the Leviathan are sitting on the rail in their Sunday clothes with plaster still in the creases of their knuckles, laughing, and arguing about whether the kraken's arms will survive the turn at Lee Circle.

skillChecks.success: Clue G1, even for a stranger: one of the plasterers, Martial Sauvinet, remembers Thursday night: the big Navy man helping dress the serpent went out at a quarter to nine and came back at ten with his trouser cuffs soaked and orange paint on his shoes, red lead from the pier, and asked for a rag and some turpentine and was very cheerful. (Automatic for Zélie, Theo or anyone they bring.)
skillChecks.failure: The plasterers are wary of white strangers on Carnival Day, and say so politely. Zélie, Theo or Pichon can get the story with a word.

skillChecks.success: Word on the street: Gravier has put six men in the Canal Street crowd tonight, 'looking for some people', and the krewe has hired extra watchmen for the float yard behind the Auditorium.
skillChecks.failure: Everybody is drunk and happy and nobody tells you anything.

scenes.name: The Den on Tchoupitoulas Street
scenes.description: Afternoon at the den. The floats are guarded; the watchmen are drinking by 3; the riders arrive from 4:30. The party can try for the packet here (see the location's secrets), take a sick rider's robe and mask from hook fourteen-nine and ride the float themselves, or simply confirm which float and which hook is Pruett's. Clovis Pinac is on his stool by the door, miserable, and this is the best moment to break him (H2): he has spent four days thinking Mr. Lucien is a murderer and that he helped hide it. Yvonne, who has known him all her life, can do it with one question.
scenes.readAloud: The den is a cotton warehouse as long as a city block, brick and timber and dusty light, and in it the eighteen floats of the Krewe of Oneiros stand nose to tail like a herd of sleeping gods, their gold leaf dull in the gloom, waiting for fire. Men in krewe armbands are sitting on cotton bales playing cards and passing a bottle. By the big door, on a stool, an old white-moustached man in a watchman's cap sits with a small dog in his lap and stares at nothing, and when he sees you he closes his eyes as if he had been expecting you and hoped you would not come.

skillChecks.success: Pinac is ready to break. He has not slept. Tell him Lucien may not have done it, and ask him who he did it for.
skillChecks.failure: An old man who will not talk to strangers about his employers. Yvonne can open him up with a word.

skillChecks.success: Robed and masked from hook fourteen-nine, you pass the krewe lieutenant as the sick rider, and you will be riding the Leviathan tonight beside the killer. (Advantage on Masking Day if already masked.)
skillChecks.failure: The lieutenant asks you the krewe's password, which you do not know; you bluff your way out, but you are not riding tonight, and Heat +1.

skillChecks.success: You reach the Leviathan's tail while the watchmen argue over a card game. With the notebook's directions, the packet is yours. Now you have to keep it.
skillChecks.failure: A watchman sees you on the wagon and Pinac's dog starts barking. You get out, but Heat +2, and Pruett will know before he robes that someone was at the serpent.

scenes.name: The Flambeaux
scenes.description: The alley behind the den, 5 to 6 p.m. Theo's welders are filling their naphtha torches. Theo explains plainly what this work is: a dollar and a half for the night and the coins the white crowd throws at their feet, carrying fire for the men who robbed them, and that they took it because they need the money and because tonight they will be walking beside the Leviathan. He has a plan if the party has not made one: two of his men will walk on either side of float fourteen; at the Canal Street halt they can make the float stop longer, or block the view, or catch what is dropped. His price is the same as Sunday's: the envelopes and the packet go together, to whoever the party chose, with the welders in the room. If the party agrees, the welders become their eyes on the route. If the party has not told Theo what they know, Pruett's paid carrier is a stranger.
scenes.readAloud: In the alley behind the den forty Black men in long white robes are filling flambeaux from a drum of naphtha by the light of a single bulb: iron frames on tall poles with four or six burners each, heavy enough that a man needs a leather cup on his belt to carry one. They talk and laugh quietly and pass a bottle, and somebody is singing under his breath, and they are men you saw on Sunday in their good suits at the Equity hall. Theo Dorsainville is checking the burners on each torch in turn, like a sergeant checking rifles. He looks up. 'A dollar and a half,' he says, 'and whatever they throw at our feet. To carry their fire down St. Charles Avenue so they can see their own faces.' He tightens a burner. 'We will be walking beside that serpent tonight. Tell me what you need.'

skillChecks.success: Theo and the carriers agree a plan with the party: two welders flank float fourteen, one ready to make the halt last, one ready to catch whatever is thrown down or dropped, and a runner to carry word to wherever the party is waiting. (No roll if the party kept its word from Sunday.)
skillChecks.failure: Theo agrees to watch the float and tell you what he sees, and no more. He has not forgotten that you have not yet said who will be paid.

encounters: Four krewe watchmen (Dockside Goons) and Clovis Pinac (Night Watchman) with Bijou (Guard Dog) at the den, only if the party is caught
A krewe lieutenant at the robing room (no combat; Deception)

acts.title: Act 2: St. Charles Avenue by Flambeau Light
acts.description: 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. The parade. The party can be in the crowd, on a balcony, on float fourteen itself in a sick man's robe, with the flambeaux, or on the far side of Canal Street with Zélie's car on Basin Street (cars cannot move on the route). Pruett makes his attempt at the long halt at Canal and St. Charles (see the parade route's secrets). If the party already has the packet, the act becomes Gravier's six men trying to take it from them in the Canal Street crowd while Pruett watches from the float. Either way it ends with a chase through half a million people. The act is a set piece: describe the light, the noise, the fire and the faces, and keep the action fast and clear.
objectives: Spot Pruett among the masked riders of float fourteen
Stop him taking or burning the packet, or take it first
Get the packet through the Canal Street crowd and away from Gravier's men

scenes.name: The Line of Fire
scenes.description: Lee Circle and down St. Charles. The floats come out of the dark one by one, each a tower of gold and color lit from below by the flambeaux, the riders masked and robed and throwing trinkets, the crowd screaming 'Throw me something, mister!' Det. Lamarque at Lee Circle can see float fourteen pass and must decide whether to leave his post (Heat +1 if he does and Lebeau hears, which he will). The party can follow the float down the avenue on foot in the crowd, which is slow (Athletics DC 12 each block to keep pace) unless someone knows the alleys behind the hotels (Knows the Block). Recognising Pruett: DC 15 Insight or Perception, or notice that one Triton on float fourteen is not throwing anything.
scenes.readAloud: They come out of the dark under the oaks like a dream someone is having about the sea. First a mounted lieutenant in a silver mask on a white horse, then the flambeaux: a double line of men in white robes, each carrying a pole with a crown of fire on it, spinning and dipping them, the flames roaring and streaming sideways, and the crowd throwing coins that ring on the pavement and the carriers catching them, scooping them, without missing a step. Then the floats, one after another, lit gold from below: a sea king on a throne, a city of drowned towers, a kraken whose arms sway as the mules lean into the turn. And then the serpent, forty feet of silver and green coiling up into the night over a mule team and a hundred raised hands, nine masked Tritons on its coils throwing glass beads into the light. Eight of them are throwing. One of them is not.

skillChecks.success: That one: the tallest Triton on the float, on the third coil near the tail, holding on with his left hand. On his right hand, in the flambeau light, a heavy gold ring.
skillChecks.failure: Nine masked figures in green on a moving serpent, against fire. You will need to be closer.

skillChecks.success: You keep pace with float fourteen through the crowd, block by block, to Canal Street.
skillChecks.failure: The crowd closes like water and you lose a block. You can catch up at the long halt at Canal Street if you run the alleys (Streetwise DC 12, or Knows the Block).

scenes.name: Float Fourteen
scenes.description: The long halt at Canal and St. Charles, eight minutes. Pruett climbs down inside the coil toward the tail, with a pocket knife. Options: a party member riding the float as the sick Triton can follow him inside the coil (a cramped fight in lath and papier-mâché twelve feet above the street, inside a moving monster: Athletics to hold on, Acrobatics to move, and Pruett has a sap); a party member on the street can climb the wagon bed from the mule side (Athletics DC 13, while the krewe lieutenant shouts); Theo's flanking carriers can refuse Pruett's torch, or catch the packet, or set the halt running long; or the party can simply let him take it and follow him. If he gets the packet into a flambeau, it burns in four rounds; someone quick can pull it out half-burned (DEX save DC 12 or 1d6 fire), and half the pages are enough. Pruett will not fight on a float in front of a hundred thousand people for longer than two rounds: he drops off the far side into the crowd and runs, and is masked, and is gone.
scenes.readAloud: At Canal Street the whole parade stops, and the noise doubles: the floats ahead are turning, the bands are playing into each other, the crowd on the neutral ground is twenty deep and screaming, and the serpent's head sways above you against the lit front of a department store. The tall Triton swings himself down off the third coil and vanishes into the serpent, into the lath and canvas of its body, like a man going down a ship's ladder into a hold. Below the tail, beside the mule team, a flambeau carrier stands very still with his torch held out, waiting, its fire roaring straight up into the dark.

skillChecks.success: Inside the coil, you reach the tail before he gets the scale off. In the roaring dark, twelve feet up, it is you and the killer and a pocket knife.
skillChecks.failure: You get stuck in the lath and canvas; by the time you are free, he has the scale off and is handing the packet out to the carrier.

skillChecks.success: On the street side, you take the packet out of the air as it drops toward the flambeau, or out of the carrier's hand, and it is under your coat before anyone on the float sees.
skillChecks.failure: Your hand closes on air. The packet is in the fire. You have four rounds.

skillChecks.success: The carrier Pruett paid is one of Theo's men, and he looks at you, and at the packet, and at Pruett's mask, and you see him decide. He swings his torch away.
skillChecks.failure: The carrier is a stranger doing a job for five dollars. He holds the torch steady.

scenes.name: Canal Street
scenes.description: Whoever has the packet must get it off Canal Street, through half a million people, past Gravier's six men, to wherever the party has arranged: Zélie's Duchess on Basin Street, the Statesman, the Equity hall, Whitcombe at the Custom House (locked and dark on Mardi Gras), or the Auditorium. Run it as a foot chase (combat.json chases): the crowd is a complication every round, masks hide everyone, and a party member with Knows the Block can make the next complication fall on a pursuer. Gravier's men will not shoot in this crowd. They use saps and fists. If Pruett got the packet and burned it, the chase is for the half-burned remains, or there is no chase, and Pruett walks away into the crowd satisfied; the party then has the photostat negatives at Crescent Photostat (if they thought of them) and the photostats in Pruett's valise (cs-scenario-004) as their remaining routes to the proof.
scenes.readAloud: Canal Street is a river of people under a sky full of neon and smoke, wall to wall, a hundred thousand faces under a hundred thousand masks, and somewhere behind you in it are six men in dock jackets who have stopped pretending to watch the parade. A brass band comes the other way, playing as loud as it can. A man on a ladder throws a fistful of confetti in your face. Somebody grabs your sleeve, laughing, and it is a stranger in a devil's mask, and you pull free, and the packet is a flat hard weight against your ribs, and the street goes on forever.

skillChecks.success: Through an arcade, a hotel kitchen and a back alley off Baronne Street, and you are clear. (Knows the Block lets one character spend it to put the next complication on a pursuer instead.)
skillChecks.failure: Dead end at a locked gate. Two of Gravier's men come round the corner behind you with saps. Fight, or go over the gate (Athletics DC 12).

skillChecks.success: You pull on a stranger's discarded mask and walk away at a parade-goer's pace, and the dock jackets go past you.
skillChecks.failure: They see you change masks. Run.

encounters: Commander Pruett inside the Leviathan (Federal Agent stats, a sap as Blackjack and a .45 automatic he will not draw in the crowd); he breaks off after two rounds
Gravier's six men on Canal Street (four Dockside Goons, two Street Toughs, saps and fists only)
Beat Cops at the corners, who arrest anyone fighting and ask questions on Ash Wednesday

acts.title: Act 3: The Ball
acts.description: 9 p.m. to 12:30 a.m. The Oneiros ball at the Municipal Auditorium, and the float yard behind it. White party members with Yvonne's invitations, Vincent's family name or Solange's cover are guests. Black party members may enter as staff (Yvonne's offer) or refuse, and the GM should honour either choice without comment: those who stay outside have the float yard, the service gate, Lebeau's driver Rigaud (H1) and the street, and some of the act's best moments. Inside: the call-outs, the Queen's court and grand march at 10, Honoré in the founder's box, Lucien masked until 11, and Pruett, unmasked and charming, from 9:30. At about 11:15, in the captain's room, Pruett and Lucien have the conversation that gives Clue G5, and Lucien understands. If Pruett did not get the packet, he tells Lucien that the party has it and that Lebeau must take it from them at dawn; if he did, he names his price for the photostats: $50,000, at 10 tomorrow morning. At midnight the police ride down Canal Street and Carnival ends. Pruett leaves at 12:10 and checks his valise at Terminal Station at 12:20.
objectives: Get into the ball, or work the outside of it
Overhear Pruett and Lucien in the captain's room
Learn, or show, that each Ste. Claire thinks the other a murderer

scenes.name: Call-Outs
scenes.description: The ballroom. The call-out section; masked krewe men calling women to dance by number; the Queen's grand march with Yvonne on her father's arm, both of them pale; Honoré in the founder's box, seventy-four, magnificent, receiving homage. The party can approach Honoré (Doors Open), who receives them with perfect courtesy and absolute contempt, and says that he will see them in his library at nine tomorrow, 'when this foolishness is over'; Solange can work the krewe men (Back Door of Every Club works on krewe men in masks as on club owners); Vincent's father Gaston, a krewe lieutenant, asks his son what in God's name he thinks he is doing. Pruett comes in at 9:30 unmasked and in white tie, greets the party by name if he has met them, and tells them, smiling, that he hopes they enjoyed the parade.
scenes.readAloud: The auditorium has been turned into the bottom of the sea. Green and silver gauze hangs from the ceiling in long rippling sheets, lit from behind so that the whole hall seems to be under moving water, and at the far end on a throne of silver shells sits a queen in white satin with a mantle eleven feet long spread down the steps like foam. Tiers of boxes go up into the dark, full of women in evening gowns and men in white tie, and on the floor the masked krewe men in their sea-god robes move among the call-out seats with numbered cards, calling women out to dance. The orchestra plays a waltz. Black waiters in white jackets go through the crowd with silver trays and nobody looks at them at all. In the founder's box an old man in white tie, upright as a mast, watches his granddaughter on her throne with an expression of complete and terrible pride.

skillChecks.success: You get yourselves to Honoré's box and have two minutes of his attention. He tells you, with perfect courtesy, that his yard has never cheated anyone who was not cheating it, that the helper rate is the custom of the river, and that if you embarrass his family he will see you ruined. He does not mention Marcel. He does not know about gang No. 9, and if you tell him now he laughs, and then looks across the hall at his son, and stops laughing.
skillChecks.failure: A lieutenant steers you away from the founder's box. Honoré has seen you, and nods, once.

skillChecks.success: Yvonne, on her throne, is watching Pruett, and Lucien, who is dancing with her, cannot stop looking at the captain's room door.
skillChecks.failure: The court is beautiful and unreadable.

scenes.name: The Captain's Room
scenes.description: About 11:15. Behind the stage, the captain's room: a bar, a long table, the krewe's old silver, the captain's chair, a window onto the float yard. Lucien comes in unmasked and drunk; Pruett follows and shuts the door. The party can hear it from the service corridor (as waiters, or by Stealth DC 12), from behind the bar as staff, from the float yard under the window, or through Yvonne, who walks in on them. The conversation (G5) should be played in full, with Lucien's realisation visible. If a party member is in the room, Pruett smiles and changes the subject, and the clue comes later from Yvonne or Lucien himself. After Pruett leaves, Lucien is alone and broken, and this is the moment a party member can reach him: Solange, Yvonne, or anyone who tells him the truth about his father's 6:10 call. He says he will go to his father at dawn.
scenes.readAloud: Through the crack of the service door you can see a long table of dark wood, old silver, a bottle, and a carved chair with a silver crown on its back. Lucien Ste. Claire is standing at the window with his mask in his hand and his face wet, and the big man in white tie is leaning on the bar, easy, pouring himself a drink. 'You told me,' Lucien says, 'that he would not be a problem.' 'And he isn't,' Pruett says pleasantly. 'My father thinks I did it. Thaddeus. My father had his car moved.' Pruett drinks. 'Then your father thinks you did it, Lucien,' he says. 'Let him. It's the most useful thing he's ever thought.' And you watch Lucien Ste. Claire understand, all at once, what he has been standing next to for three years, and sit down in the captain's chair as if his legs had been cut.

skillChecks.success: You hear all of it from the service corridor, and get away before the door opens.
skillChecks.failure: You hear the first two lines and a krewe lieutenant comes down the corridor. You are a waiter, or a guest who is lost; Deception DC 12, or Heat +1 and you are put out of the building.

skillChecks.success: Alone with Lucien afterward, you get him to say it: he ran gang No. 9 with Gravier and Pruett; he did not kill Marcel; he thought his father had. He will go to Esplanade Avenue at dawn and tell his father everything. (Automatic for Yvonne or Solange.)
skillChecks.failure: Lucien weeps, drinks, and says nothing you can use. He goes to the Café Isabeau after midnight, where Solange or Ulysse can find him.

scenes.name: Midnight on Canal Street
scenes.description: At midnight a line of mounted police rides slowly down Canal Street from the river, and behind them come the street sweepers, and the crowd goes home. Masks come off. Carnival is over. Pruett leaves the Auditorium at 12:10 in a cab and goes to Terminal Station, where at 12:20 he checks a heavy valise (claim check 4471) and then walks back to the Hotel Vauclain. A tail (Stealth vs his passive Perception 14, three successes before three failures; a Shadow needs two) sees all of it. If the party has the packet, they must also decide where to keep it until noon tomorrow; every safe place in the city is closed, and Lebeau knows they have it. Theo offers the Equity hall's cellar. Mrs. Barthé offers the Statesman's press room. Whitcombe, telephoned at the Vauclain, offers his own room, two floors below Pruett's. End the scenario on the sweepers and the quiet, and the first church bell of Ash Wednesday.
scenes.readAloud: At midnight the music stops all at once, as if someone had lifted the needle off a record, and down Canal Street from the river comes a slow line of mounted policemen, shoulder to shoulder, the horses' hooves loud on the pavement, and the crowd parts in front of them and goes, laughing and stumbling and holding each other up. Behind the horses come the street sweepers, a dozen men with push brooms and a water wagon, through a sea of paper and beads and broken glass and lost masks. In five minutes the widest street in America is empty under its neon. Somewhere a bell begins to ring. It is Ash Wednesday, and the books close at noon.

skillChecks.success: You tail Pruett from the Auditorium to Terminal Station and watch him check a heavy brown valise at the baggage room and put the claim check, 4471, in his wallet. Then he walks back to the Vauclain, whistling.
skillChecks.failure: He sees you on Basin Street, tips his hat, and gets into a cab. You do not know where he went, but the baggage clerk at Terminal Station will remember a big man with a Navy ring if you ask tomorrow.

encounters: No planned fight at the ball. If the party starts one, Lebeau and a dozen police are in the building.

In the float yard behind the Auditorium, if Pruett did not get the packet on the route: two krewe watchmen (Dockside Goons) and Pruett himself, briefly, at about 10:30, checking the Leviathan's tail; the outside team's moment
Pruett on the street after midnight (no fight; he will not risk one; a tail)

npcsInvolved.name: Commander Thaddeus Pruett, 54
npcsInvolved.role: The killer, masked on float fourteen
npcsInvolved.description: In a Triton's green satin robe and silver-scaled mask on the parade; in white tie at the ball. Courteous, amused, unhurried, never once raising his voice. Use Federal Agent stats with a sap and a .45 automatic.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Burn the packet, sell the photostats to Lucien for $50,000 at 10 tomorrow, see the settlement signed at noon and catch the 1:15 train.

npcsInvolved.name: Lucien Ste. Claire, 47
npcsInvolved.role: Secret captain of the Krewe of Oneiros
npcsInvolved.description: Masked and robed as the captain until 11, then unmasked, drunk and falling apart. Dances the grand march with his daughter and cannot look at her.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Until 11:15, to survive. After it, to tell his father the truth.

npcsInvolved.name: Honoré Ste. Claire, 74
npcsInvolved.role: Founder of the yard and of the krewe's modern glory
npcsInvolved.description: Tall, upright as a mast, white hair, white tie, a voice that has never had to be raised. Courteous, contemptuous, devoted to his family and certain of his place. Believes his son is a murderer and will protect him anyway.
npcsInvolved.motivation: His granddaughter's night, his son's freedom, his family's name.

npcsInvolved.name: Yvonne Ste. Claire, 20
npcsInvolved.description: In white satin and an eleven-foot mantle on a throne of shells, pale and furious and brave. Companion (see her sheet). Can go anywhere in the building tonight.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To know, and then to act.

npcsInvolved.name: Clovis Pinac, 66
npcsInvolved.role: Night watchman, lent to the krewe's den
npcsInvolved.description: Has not slept since Friday. Ready to break.

npcsInvolved.name: Martial Sauvinet, 44
npcsInvolved.description: Lean, quick, a Carnival Day straw hat and plaster in his knuckles. Saw Pruett come back with wet cuffs on Thursday night.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To enjoy his Carnival, and, once he understands, to see the man hang.

npcsInvolved.name: Ulysse Arceneaux, 58
npcsInvolved.description: Bald, white-jacketed, a perfect memory and a perfect silence, both for sale to friends.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Solange, whom he regards as a daughter, and a good tip.

npcsInvolved.name: Patrolman Denis Rigaud, 26
npcsInvolved.description: Young, bored, talkative, waiting by the car outside the Auditorium with a sack of peanuts.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To go home. Will gossip to anyone who shares the peanuts.

npcsInvolved.name: Gaston Lamarque, 64
npcsInvolved.role: Cotton factor; a lieutenant of the Krewe of Oneiros; Vincent's father
npcsInvolved.description: Silver-haired, correct, frightened for his son and for his own standing. Not a villain; a man of his class.
npcsInvolved.motivation: That his son not ruin himself, or the family, in front of the krewe.

rewards.money: Nobody pays the party on Mardi Gras. Coins thrown at the flambeaux are the carriers', not the party's. If the party rode float fourteen, the krewe's trinkets in their robe pockets are worth about $3. Pruett's wallet, if anyone gets it, holds $140 and claim check 4471.
items: The oilcloth packet: the Navy-copy pay summaries for three years and the colored-window envelope register, whole or half-burned (Clues D2, D3, E1 in Marcel's hand and the yard's; the proof)
Possibly a Triton's robe and mask from hook fourteen-nine
The knowledge of claim check 4471 at Terminal Station, if Pruett was tailed
Lucien Ste. Claire's word that he will go to his father at dawn

twists: The killer rides on top of the evidence. Pruett moved himself onto float fourteen on Monday, and on Mardi Gras night he is masked, anonymous and twelve feet above the crowd, with the proof under his feet.
The flambeaux carriers are the welders the fraud robbed, carrying fire for the men who robbed them, and at the moment that matters one of them chooses whether the proof burns.

Each Ste. Claire believes the other is a murderer and has been covering for him for four days. Lucien learns the truth from the killer's own mouth, in the captain's room of his own krewe, and the realisation is the hinge of the campaign.

Nothing can be filed on Mardi Gras. Even if the party holds the packet at 8 p.m., they must keep it, and themselves, until the Custom House opens on Ash Wednesday, with the police captain and the waterfront both knowing they have it.

If Pruett burns the packet, he has not won: the photostats he took from Marcel's briefcase are in a valise at Terminal Station, and the negatives are in a drawer at Crescent Photostat on Carondelet Street. He does not know about the negatives.
dmTips: This is the set-piece scenario. Budget about an hour for Act 1, an hour and a half for Act 2 and an hour and a half for Act 3. The expected fights are inside the Leviathan (brief) and on Canal Street (a chase with fists and saps). Nobody shoots in this crowd, and the GM should make that plain.

Describe Carnival with love. It is the first since the war, people are joyful, and the joy is real. Then show, without comment, who walks beside the floats carrying the fire and who rides on top throwing glass beads. The players will draw the conclusion; do not draw it for them.

The color line decides who can enter the ball. Do not make the Black characters' players sit out: give the outside team the float yard, Lebeau's driver, the street, the Café Isabeau and the tail to Terminal Station, which are where several clues are. If a Black character goes in as staff, play it straight and let it be as galling as it was, and give them the run of the service corridors, which go everywhere.
Never put Theo's welders in danger to give the party something to rescue. They are on the route doing a job and pursuing their own plan, and they choose whether to help at each moment.

Clue G5 in the captain's room is the scene that breaks the case open. Give it in full, and let the players see Lucien understand. If nobody is in a position to overhear it, have Yvonne walk in on it, and come out and tell them, shaking.
If the party got the packet on Monday, swap the logic of Act 2: Pruett and Gravier's men hunt the party on the route and at the ball, and the float is a decoy. The captain's room scene still happens.

Track Heat. Masking Day protects anyone masked and unrecognised, but fights in front of police (+2), being thrown out of the ball (+1) and breaking into the den (+2) still count. By midnight Lebeau should know exactly who has the packet.
